messages:
marco: Heads-up: new hotpatch exception process for the release train effective next week. We had a couple of surprises last cycle so this tightens the loop.
tess: Can you summarize the main changes?
marco: TL;DR: faster triage, stricter acceptance gates, and an exec notification on any exception. Key points below.
release-lead: Exception types: emergency-security, production-p0, data-corruption. Non-critical bugfixes are not exceptions.
sre-oncall: Acceptance gates now include an automated smoke matrix run + an explicit perf gate: p95 must be within 10% of baseline for 10m after deploy. If violated, auto-abort happens.
marco: We also require a 2-person approval for any hotpatch after freeze: release-lead + oncall. Approvals should be recorded via the exception form link.
cto-bot: Exec notice: CTO requests "rapid visibility" on exceptions. Any exception must trigger a short summary to execs (auto email) with severity, rollback plan, and SLA impact estimate.
tess: Where's the exception form?
marco: Form: https://confluence.redwood/releases/hotpatch-exception (internal) — includes fields for reason, impact, rollback steps, and risk mitigations.
sre-oncall: Deploy hooks updated: before any exception merge a preflight job runs: \n```\n./ci/preflight-hotpatch --smoke --perf --static-checks\n```\nIf preflight fails, it blocks the merge.
release-lead: Canary cadence for hotpatches is conservative: 0.5% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% with 15m observation windows.
marco: For private/dedicated customers: if the hotpatch touches routing or auth layers, we will notify affected customers via the customer-notify list before the patch lands.
sre-oncall: Alerts to watch: p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, auth-failures, route-lookup-hitratio, db-write-failures. Auto-abort triggers on p95 > baseline*1.1 for 10m OR error_rate increase >0.7% sustained for 5m.
tess: Who owns rollback when an auto-abort happens?
release-lead: Auto-abort triggers an incident and the rollback lead is the deploy owner of the change; release-lead coordinates customer comms. If the deploy owner is unavailable, oncall initiates rollback.
cto-bot: Exec ask: include an estimated MTTD/MTTR in the exception ticket for any hotpatch. Helps leadership prioritize.
marco: Small operational note: soft freeze starts 2026-01-10T22:00:00Z before the release train; exceptions must be filed before that cutoff or be emergency-only.
sre-oncall: I've added a dashboard for hotpatch metrics and a playbook link. Will post the URL here once available.
release-lead: Also adding a short post-exception blameless note requirement: 3-4 lines summarizing why the exception was needed and what we'll change to avoid repetition. Due within 48h.
tess: Nice. That'll help our retros.
deploy-bot: Hotpatch exception workflow updated in CI: preflight -> approval -> canary -> notify.
marco: Thanks everyone. Please read the doc and update your oncall rotations if you expect exceptions during your shift. Tag this thread id 2061234567 for follow-ups.
sre-oncall: Acknowledged. Will post dashboard URL and any alerts during the next window.
release-lead: Closing loop: template for exec summary added to the confluence page so it's quick to fill.
tess: Ack. :white_check_mark:
